chapters.title: How it happened that Mastro Cherry, carpenter, found a piece of wood that wept and laughed like a child.
chapters.routing_description: Mastro Cherry tries to cut a log that cries and laughs, frightening him into a faint.

chapters.title: Mastro Cherry gives the piece of wood to his friend Geppetto, who takes it to make himself a Marionette that will dance, fence, and turn somersaults.
chapters.routing_description: A talking log provokes fights between Mastro Cherry and Geppetto before Geppetto takes it home to make a performing Marionette.

chapters.title: As soon as he gets home, Geppetto fashions the Marionette and calls it Pinocchio. The first pranks  of the Marionette.
chapters.routing_description: Geppetto carves and names Pinocchio, who steals his wig and runs away; a Carabineer arrests Geppetto after the crowd intervenes.

chapters.title: The story of Pinocchio and the Talking Cricket, in which one sees that bad children do not like to be corrected by those who know more than they do.
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio rejects the Talking Cricket’s advice about obedience, study and work, then kills him with a hammer.

chapters.title: Pinocchio is hungry and looks for an egg to cook himself an omelet; but, to his surprise, the omelet flies out of the window.
chapters.routing_description: Hungry Pinocchio searches for food and tries to cook an egg, but a live Chick emerges and flies away.

chapters.title: Pinocchio falls asleep with his feet on a foot warmer, and awakens the next day with his feet all burned off.
chapters.routing_description: An old man drenches the hungry Pinocchio with water; back home, his feet burn away while he sleeps beside the stove.

chapters.title: Geppetto returns home and gives his own breakfast to the Marionette
chapters.routing_description: Geppetto climbs through the window to reach the footless Pinocchio and gives him three pears, including their skins and cores.

chapters.title: Geppetto makes Pinocchio a new pair of feet, and sells his coat to buy him an A-B-C book.
chapters.routing_description: Geppetto makes new feet and simple clothes for Pinocchio, then sells his coat to buy an A-B-C book.

chapters.title: Pinocchio sells his A-B-C book to pay his way into the Marionette Theater.
chapters.routing_description: Music draws Pinocchio away from school; he sells his A-B-C book to a ragpicker for four pennies to enter the theater.

chapters.title: The Marionettes recognize their brother Pinocchio, and greet him with loud cheers; but the Director, Fire Eater, happens along and poor Pinocchio almost loses his life.
chapters.routing_description: The Marionettes welcome Pinocchio and interrupt their performance; Fire Eater orders him brought to the kitchen as firewood.

chapters.title: Fire Eater sneezes and forgives Pinocchio, who saves his friend, Harlequin, from death.
chapters.routing_description: Fire Eater spares Pinocchio but threatens Harlequin; Pinocchio offers himself in his friend’s place and wins both their pardons.

chapters.title: Fire Eater gives Pinocchio five gold pieces for his father, Geppetto; but the Marionette meets a Fox and a Cat and follows them.
chapters.routing_description: Fire Eater gives Pinocchio five gold pieces for Geppetto; a Fox and Cat lure him with promises of multiplying money in the Field of Wonders.

chapters.title: The Inn of the Red Lobster
chapters.routing_description: The Fox and Cat leave Pinocchio to pay their inn bill; setting out alone at midnight, he ignores the Talking Cricket’s ghost warning of swindlers and Assassins.

chapters.title: Pinocchio, not having listened to the good advice of the Talking Cricket, falls into the hands of the Assassins.
chapters.routing_description: Two masked Assassins chase Pinocchio for the coins under his tongue; he bites off a cat’s paw and escapes a burning pine tree and muddy pool.

chapters.title: The Assassins chase Pinocchio, catch him, and hang him to the branch of a giant oak tree.
chapters.routing_description: A maiden with azure hair refuses Pinocchio shelter; the Assassins catch him, fail to stab his wooden body, and hang him from an oak.

chapters.title: The Lovely Maiden with Azure Hair sends for the poor Marionette, puts him to bed, and calls three Doctors to tell her if Pinocchio is dead or alive.
chapters.routing_description: The Fairy sends a Falcon and Medoro to rescue Pinocchio; a Crow, Owl and Talking Cricket debate whether he is alive until he weeps.

chapters.title: Pinocchio eats sugar, but refuses to take medicine. When the undertakers come for him, he drinks the medicine and feels better. Afterwards he tells a lie and, in punishment, his nose grows longer and longer.
chapters.routing_description: Black Rabbits with a coffin persuade Pinocchio to take his medicine; lies about the gold pieces make his nose too long to pass through the door.

chapters.title: Pinocchio finds the Fox and the Cat again, and goes with them to sow the gold pieces in the Field of Wonders.
chapters.routing_description: Woodpeckers shorten Pinocchio’s nose, but on his way to meet Geppetto he follows the Fox and Cat and buries four coins in the Field of Wonders.
locations: City of Simple Simons and Field of Wonders

chapters.title: Pinocchio is robbed of his gold pieces and, in punishment, is sentenced to four months in prison.
chapters.routing_description: A Parrot reveals that the Fox and Cat stole the buried gold; a Gorilla judge imprisons Pinocchio, who gains release by calling himself a thief.

chapters.title: Freed from prison, Pinocchio sets out to return to the Fairy; but on the way he meets a Serpent and later is caught in a trap.
chapters.routing_description: Returning toward the Fairy, Pinocchio meets a smoking-tailed Serpent that dies laughing, then is trapped while trying to take grapes.

chapters.title: Pinocchio is caught by a Farmer, who uses him as a watchdog for his chicken coop.
chapters.routing_description: A Glowworm rebukes the trapped Pinocchio for stealing grapes; the Farmer chains him in place of his dead watchdog Melampo.

chapters.title: Pinocchio discovers the thieves and, as a reward for faithfulness, he regains his liberty.
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio refuses the Weasels’ bribe, traps them in the henhouse and earns his freedom, keeping the dead Melampo’s collusion secret.

chapters.title: Pinocchio weeps upon learning that the Lovely Maiden with Azure Hair is dead. He meets a Pigeon, who carries him to the seashore. He throws himself into the sea to go to the aid of his father.
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio mourns at the Fairy’s tombstone; a Pigeon carries him to the coast, where he dives after Geppetto’s sinking boat.

chapters.title: Pinocchio reaches the Island of the Busy Bees and finds the Fairy once more.
chapters.routing_description: Washed onto an island, Pinocchio hears a Dolphin’s warning about the Shark, refuses work, then carries a woman’s water and recognizes the Fairy.

chapters.title: Pinocchio promises the Fairy to be good and to study, as he is growing tired of being a Marionette, and wishes to become a real boy.
chapters.routing_description: The grown Fairy becomes Pinocchio’s mother and promises he can become a boy if he obeys, studies and works.

chapters.title: Pinocchio goes to the seashore with his friends to see the Terrible Shark.
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio wins respect at school and studies well, but classmates tempt him to skip lessons to see a supposed Shark at the shore.
locations: school and road to the seashore

chapters.title: The great battle between Pinocchio and his playmates. One is wounded. Pinocchio is arrested.
chapters.routing_description: Classmates fight Pinocchio with schoolbooks and wound Eugene; the Carabineers arrest Pinocchio, who escapes while retrieving his cap.

chapters.title: Pinocchio runs the danger of being fried in a pan like a fish
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio rescues the pursuing Alidoro from drowning, then a Green Fisherman catches him in a net and prepares to fry him as a fish.

chapters.title: Pinocchio returns to the Fairy’s house and she promises him that, on the morrow, he will cease to be a Marionette and become a boy. A wonderful party of coffee-and-milk to celebrate the great event.
chapters.routing_description: Alidoro rescues Pinocchio from the frying pan; after a long wait for the Snail and another forgiveness, Pinocchio excels at school and the Fairy plans his transformation party.

chapters.title: Pinocchio, instead of becoming a boy, runs away to the Land of Toys with his friend, Lamp-Wick.
chapters.routing_description: While delivering party invitations, Pinocchio finds Lamp-Wick waiting for the Land of Toys wagon and stays past his promised return time, tempted by endless holidays.

chapters.title: After five months of play, Pinocchio wakes up one fine morning and finds a great surprise awaiting him.
chapters.routing_description: Pinocchio joins Lamp-Wick in the wagon, hears a donkey’s warning and watches the driver bite its ears; in the Land of Toys they spend five months playing.

chapters.title: Pinocchio’s ears become like those of a Donkey. In a little while he changes into a real Donkey and begins to bray.
chapters.routing_description: A Dormouse diagnoses Pinocchio’s growing ears as donkey fever; he and Lamp-Wick hide their ears, laugh at each other, then turn into donkeys.

chapters.title: Pinocchio, having become a Donkey, is bought by the owner of a Circus, who wants to teach him to do tricks. The Donkey becomes lame and is sold to a man who wants to use his skin for a drumhead.
chapters.routing_description: Sold to a circus, the donkey Pinocchio is trained by beatings, sees the Fairy in the audience and becomes lame; a buyer throws him into the sea for his skin.

chapters.title: Pinocchio is thrown into the sea, eaten by fishes, and becomes a Marionette once more. As he swims to land, he is swallowed by the Terrible Shark.
chapters.routing_description: Fish eat away Pinocchio’s donkey covering and restore his wooden form; he escapes his buyer but is swallowed by the Shark while swimming toward an azure Goat.

chapters.title: In the Shark’s body Pinocchio finds whom? Read this chapter, my children, and you will know.
chapters.routing_description: Inside the Shark, Pinocchio reunites with Geppetto, who survived on a swallowed ship’s supplies; after a failed attempt, he carries his father out through the sleeping Shark’s mouth.

chapters.title: Pinocchio finally ceases to be a Marionette and becomes a boy
chapters.routing_description: The Tunny brings father and son ashore; Pinocchio cares for Geppetto, sees Lamp-Wick die, works and studies, and gives his savings to the Fairy before waking as a real boy.
locations: shore, straw cottage and Farmer John’s farm
